accepted.question_text: Does there exist a polynomial f(x,y) with rational coefficients such that the induced map f: Q x Q -> Q is a bijection, meaning that for every rational number q there is exactly one pair of rational numbers (x,y) with f(x,y)=q?

evidence.quote: Is there any polynomial f(x,y)\in{\mathbb Q}[x,y]{} such that f\colon\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q} \rightarrow\mathbb{Q} is a bijection?
